findings.rule: Resolve stor[T + c] by first expanding a temporary T that is defined as sha3(k, s): if s is a known mapping of structs, this is member c of s[k] (stor4[k].field_(256*c)), never an array at slot c indexed by the hash; only infer 'array at slot c' when the index is not itself a sha3 result.

findings.issue: The keccak scratch writes behind every mapping access are printed (1510 lines, a quarter of the noise of this text), often twice in a row with the same values, though every sha3 that reads them is already printed with its arguments. They survive only in the functions where the free-memory pointer later becomes a phi (the P2 cause), so a later read at mem[mem[64] + k] is not proven disjoint from mem[0..63].
findings.rule: A store overwritten by a later store to the same address with no read in between is dead. Track the invariant mem[64] >= 128 (true when every store to mem[64] stores 128, or mem[64] plus a non-negative size below 2^64): then mem[mem[64] + k] (k >= 0) never reads [0, 64), and scratch stores whose only readers are folded sha3 are dead.

findings.source: BondingManager.sol:1037-1052 if (del.bondedAmount == 0) return Unbonded; else if (del.startRound > currentRound()) return Pending; else return Bonded;
findings.issue: The enum return is printed as a memory return whose start and length are built from a phi of the free-memory pointer, instead of 'return _7'. In each arm _8 equals the value just stored in mem[64], so the length is 32 and the word is _7.
findings.rule: When each predecessor of a join assigns the phi _8 the same expression it stores to mem[64], fold _8 - mem[64] to 0; 'mem[p] = v; return memory from p len 32' is 'return v'.

notes: Large functions (bond 1047 lines, bondWithHint, bondForWithHint 1265, rebond*, unbond*, reward*, slashTranscoder, transferBond 1800) reviewed by structure: control flow, external calls, storage writes, events (event list per function matches the source paths of tryToJoinActiveSet, resignTranscoder, updateDelegatorWithEarnings, processRebond), reverts. Read in full: the getters, setters, delegatorStatus, withdrawStake, transcoder, claimEarnings, withdrawFees (head and tail), pendingFees; no semantic error found (pendingStakeAndFees, ensureInitializedCumulativeFactorsPool and updateDelegatorWithEarnings match, including the unused stake overflow check kept in pendingFees). Same code: bond = bondWithHint = bondForWithHint with msg.sender/zero hints; rebondWithHint/rebond, rebondFromUnbonded*/rebond*, unbondWithHint/unbond, rewardWithHint/reward/rewardForTranscoder* differ only in hints or the caller check. Loops: the source loops of SortedDoublyLL (descendList, ascendList) are in the public library, reached by DELEGATECALL to the link address 0x1150a32330fd1f3eca03515f48069c69742f5164 (a link placeholder of the build, not an error), so they are not in this bytecode and not counted; no implicit loop either. 93 of the 119 library delegatecalls and most controller/minter/roundsManager calls lose their names and arguments after the first if-join (P2, 386 lines). The delegators mapping is named transcoderTotalStake after the getter of its member delegatedAmount (P13). SafeMath.sub2 is the contract's own require 'insufficient fees to withdraw' merged with the checked sub (exact). Event names TransferBond/TreasuryReward/RewardCallerSet and the library function names are not in the signature database (normal).
summary: Faithful, but hard to read: after the first if-join the free-memory pointer is unknown, so most calls lose their names (P2), 1510 keccak scratch writes and the zeroing of memory structs stay in the text, and transcoders[t].lastFeeRound shows as an invented array stor10 indexed by a hash.
